item.title: Grocer-turned-lawmaker says Mamdani’s government-run stores 'might not even last a year’
item.description: Rep. Mike Rulli, a former grocer, warns Zohran Mamdani's government-run grocery stores will bleed red and put hundreds of small businesses out.
item.content:encoded:
A former grocer is joining the chorus of criticism against New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's plan for government-run grocery stores, arguing it would harm hundreds of small businesses forced to compete with them.

"That supermarket will just bleed red the entire time it's open, from the first time you turn the key until it closes," Rep. Mike Rulli, R-Ohio, told Fox News Digital. "And I would bet the farm there's no way these grocery stores last more than five years — they might not even last a year."

Rulli grew up with his family's Ohio-based grocery store chain, Rulli Brothers, which is now run by his brothers.

EXPERTS SCORCH MAMDANI'S GROCERY PLAN AS AN 'ILLUSION' THAT WILL HAVE TAXPAYERS FOOTING THE BILL

Rulli said his family's small but thriving two-location business has given him an appreciation for the challenges facing small business owners in New York City, whom he argued would be harmed by competition from Mamdani's city-run stores.

"You will put hundreds of these small businesses out of business. And a lot of these businesses are owned by immigrants," Rulli said. "So I mean, I don't think the mayor could possibly have asked for a worse situation."

NY GOVERNOR HOPEFUL VOWS SHOWDOWN WITH MAMDANI OVER SOCIALIST AGENDA: ‘I WILL STOP HIM’

Mamdani, the Democratic socialist mayor of New York City, unveiled a plan for government-funded grocery stores while on the campaign trail. The city has since committed $70 million to constructing one store in each of the five boroughs, with an aim to open all five by 2030.

Mamdani discussed the agreement during a recent news conference, saying, "Once a month, our five city-run grocery stores will set prices for this core set of goods at 30% below typical retail prices."

MAMDANI’S CITY GROCERY PLAN COULD LEAVE TAXPAYERS PAYING FOR EVERY BANANA

While the plan has been cheered by progressives, it has been panned by business groups such as the Multicultural Business Coalition, which the New York Post reported was threatening to sue Mamdani.

Rulli, noting that grocery stores already operate on thin profit margins, said Mamdani's government shops will likely be "operating at a loss the entire time."

"When you think about the grocery industry, [it] runs on about 27% gross. That's before you pay your bills. Once you pay your bills, you're about one-and-a-quarter, one-and-half-percent net," he said.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

That, he argued, would make it a drain on taxpayers as long as they remained open.

"This is the biggest mistake the mayor has made," Rulli said.

item.title: MIKE PENCE: Congress must finish Lindsey Graham’s fight against Putin
item.description: The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act targets Putin's shadow fleet, energy exports and sanctions evasion funding the Ukraine war.
item.content:encoded:
Freedom has lost one of its fiercest defenders, and I have lost a dear friend.

For more than three decades, South Carolina Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham stood at the center of the great debates over our nation’s security and America’s role in the world. He understood that peace is preserved not by wishful thinking, but by American strength. He knew that dictators are not pacified by concessions, but deterred by unshakable resolve.

History will remember his many accomplishments. The Senate has already taken an important step toward securing one more by overwhelmingly advancing his legislation. Now it must complete its work, and the House must act without delay.

GRAHAM'S FINAL MISSION ADVANCES AS SENATE MOVES TO CRUSH PUTIN'S WAR MACHINE WITH RUSSIA, IRAN SANCTIONS

Congress has an opportunity to ensure that one of his greatest achievements is still to come.

The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 is more than just another sanctions bill. It is the culmination of Lindsey’s determined effort to deny Russian President Vladimir Putin the money, technology and international support fueling Russia’s brutal and unconscionable war against Ukraine. Passing it would not simply honor his memory. It would advance the cause to which he devoted the final chapter of his public life.

More than four years after Russia launched its unprovoked war of conquest, Putin continues to finance his war machine through energy exports, financial networks and an elaborate system of sanctions evasion. Existing sanctions have imposed real costs, but they have not been enough. Putin and his henchmen have adapted. Russia has built a shadow fleet of ships to move its oil around the world. It has relied on foreign companies to sustain its defense-industrial base. And too many nations continue to purchase Russian energy with their money while condemning Russian aggression with their words.

Lindsey understood that half-measures would never change Putin’s calculations.

REPORT WARNS RUSSIA USING SHADOW FLEET TO PROBE NATO DRONE DEFENSES

His legislation would impose mandatory sanctions on Russia’s political leadership, financial institutions, state-owned energy enterprises and the networks helping Moscow evade existing restrictions. It would target the shadow fleet transporting Russian oil, tighten financial and export controls, and use targeted tariffs to encourage the world’s largest purchasers of Russian energy to end their support for the Kremlin’s war machine. Just as importantly, it preserves presidential waiver authority when a waiver serves America’s national interest, ensuring that strength remains guided by sound judgment.

At its heart, this legislation is about restoring the deterrence that keeps dictators from mistaking American restraint for weakness.

History has taught us repeatedly that unchecked aggression only invites more aggression. Every barrel of oil sold through sanctions evasion, every financial transaction that slips through the cracks and every dollar flowing into the Kremlin’s coffers help finance missiles and drones that rain terror on Ukrainian cities and encourage other authoritarian regimes to test the resolve of the free world.

ZELENSKYY SAYS PUTIN 'LOST THE INITIATIVE' AS UKRAINE'S TECH INDUSTRY RESHAPES THE WAR

Lindsey Graham believed America should never shrink from that challenge. He knew that the United States must lead, our allies must stand together and our adversaries must know that freedom has both the will and the means to defend itself.

One of Lindsey’s last acts in public life was to travel to Kyiv and meet with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to express America’s continued support for the long-suffering Ukrainian people. He believed this legislation could help bring Putin to the negotiating table and hasten the day when this terrible war finally ends. I believe he was right.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Congress can pay tribute to Lindsey Graham with eloquent speeches and heartfelt memorials. Those are certainly fitting. But the tribute that would matter most to Lindsey would be finishing the work he began.

It’s time for Congress to pass the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. Let’s complete his final mission.

item.title: Rand Paul's calls for Fauci to to face imprisonment continue after contentious hearing
item.description: Sen. Rand Paul said Anthony Fauci lied to Congress about gain-of-function research last week and should face felony charges if convicted of the serious crime.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., has frequently suggested that Dr. Anthony Fauci should face prison time, and he was still open to the idea Tuesday when pressed about his past calls on that front.

Paul spoke on MS NOW about his response to the former director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases invoking the Fifth Amendment more than 100 times during a Senate hearing chaired by Paul last week.

The Republican senator admitted that he didn't know what to expect from Fauci's testimony, arguing that Fauci likely could have escaped legal culpability under former President Joe Biden's pardon. Geist remarked that Fauci, under the guidance of his lawyers, likely wanted to avoid speaking to Paul, who has advocated for him to be jailed. He followed up by asking if he still believes in that.

CAN FAUCI HIDE BEHIND THE FIFTH? GAME-CHANGING BIDEN PARDON MAY NOT PROVIDE COMPLETE COVER, EXPERTS SAY

"That's a good question," Paul said. "Did he lie to Congress? I think he did lie to Congress. And I think, to be fair, that people who lie to Congress should be charged with a felony and, if convicted, go to jail. That’s also a felony crime. So I think both destroying records and lying to Congress are serious crimes."

Paul explained that it was more important to him to learn the truth about the gain-of-function research allegedly connected to Fauci prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Geist then asked if anyone else should face a criminal investigation. Paul stopped short of suggesting legal ramifications but added that they "should all apologize" and were culpable in other ways.

Turning back to Fauci, Geist asked Paul if he believed the doctor had some "nefarious" purpose behind his actions.

WATCH: RAND PAUL SAYS THERE'S ONE THING AMERICANS HAVE NEVER HEARD FROM FAUCI

"I would say it's wrongheaded. I'm not sure I would use the word 'nefarious.' I would say that he is of the belief that the common man can't handle the truth, and that people like him who are the science, the elite, and the experts should make decisions," Paul said, pointing to Fauci's shifting comments regarding masks.

He added that Fauci was telling "lies, platonic lies, because he's one of the philosopher kings. So it really is about an attitude, but it is an arrogance, and it is an arrogance that shouldn't go unchallenged."

Fox News Digital reached out to Fauci and Paul's office for further comment.

RAND PAUL SEEKS CONTEMPT CHARGES AFTER FAUCI INVOKES FIFTH AMENDMENT MORE THAN 100 TIMES

In 2021, Paul told "Hannity" that lying about gain-of-function research is a felony "punishable by five years in jail." The controversial method refers to manipulating or altering an organism or virus for purposes of research, which could give it enhanced abilities.

"We’ve referred it to the Department of Justice," Paul said. "I don’t think Biden’s Department of Justice will do anything with it but yes, it is very dangerous to have public officials who we need to have trust in coming and lying to us, but he has lied dozens of times."

Paul directly told Fox News' Laura Ingraham in 2024 that Fauci's consequence should be jail.

"I think he lied to Congress, which is a felony. You know, several folks from the Trump administration were accused of lying to Congress and carted off to jail with FBI agents all over the property, host, you know, yanking them out of their house early in the morning," he said. "But Anthony Fauci did lie to Congress. We know that from his own words, not because I say lies, but his private email say he was lying. Virtually everything he said in private contradicted what he was saying in public."

item.title: GOP Rep Chuck Edwards drops re-election bid after House ethics report recommends censure
item.description: Republican Rep. Chuck Edwards of North Carolina dropped his re-election bid in the wake of the release of a House Ethics Committee report.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., announced early on Wednesday morning that he was dropping his re-election bid.

"After much prayer and reflection, I’ve decided to withdraw from my re-election campaign. I will complete my current term. Serving Western North Carolina has been the honor of my life. Thank you for your trust, prayers, and support. God bless WNC and America," Edwards noted in a post on X that was published at 3:32 a.m. ET.

The announcement came two days after the House Ethics Committee released a report recommending Edwards' censure.

GOP LAWMAKER'S GIFTS, 'EFFUSIVE AFFECTION' TOWARD YOUNG STAFFERS DETAILED IN EXPLOSIVE ETHICS REPORT

Fox News Digital reached out to Edwards' congressional office and campaign on Wednesday morning.

Edwards has served in the U.S. House of Representatives since early 2023.

He decisively won the GOP primary in North Carolina's 11th Congressional District earlier this year.

'MCDONALD'S CHANGED THE COURSE OF MY LIFE': CONGRESSMAN SELLS BUSINESS HE BUILT SINCE HIS TEEN YEARS

But on Monday, the House Committee on Ethics issued a report finding Edwards "engaged in persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct towards two young female staffers."

While Edwards "denied that any of his conduct was intended as a sexual or romantic advance, his pattern of behavior would lead a reasonable observer to interpret it as such, including providing the young women with lavish and recurrent gifts, making comments regarding their appearance and dress, inviting them to intimate dinners and vacations, sending notes regarding his effusive affection, and inviting them to other activities as a way to spend time together," the report says.

The committee said it found "no evidence that Representative Edwards engaged in sexual activity with or explicitly propositioned any individual under his employ."

Edwards "was aware, however, that his excessive attention toward the young women had led to rumors and innuendo in the office," the report says. "Both women were uncomfortable with his behavior (which they attempted to communicate) but were put in an untenable position by virtue of his status as their boss and a Member of Congress. Representative Edwards was at minimum blind to that reality, and at worst, dismissive of the impact his inappropriate conduct had on the careers and wellbeing of two women on his staff."

REPUBLICAN LAWMAKER WELCOMES HOUSE ETHICS PROBE INTO SEXUAL MISCONDUCT ALLEGATIONS AGAINST HIM

"The Committee hereby adopts this Report in this matter and recommends Representative Edwards be censured for his conduct," the document noted.

item.title: Archaeologists uncover sprawling Roman estate buried for centuries beneath farmland
item.description: The fourth-century Roman villa in Devon, in the U.K., yielded a striking mosaic, a copper-alloy bracelet, an engraved gemstone and an elaborate bathhouse complex.
item.content:encoded:
Archaeologists in the United Kingdom recently uncovered the remains of a sprawling ancient Roman villa dating back over 1,600 years.

The fourth-century villa was found on farmland between the villages of Halberton and Sampford Peverell in Devon.

The excavation was led by the Saving Halberton's Ancient Roman Environment (SHARE) project, a partnership between the University of Exeter and Cotswold Archaeology, as news agency SWNS noted. 

RARE PAGAN MASTERPIECE EMERGES NEAR WHERE ST PAUL SPREAD TEACHINGS OF CHRISTIANITY

The star of the excavation was an ornate Roman mosaic made of thousands of tiny stone cubes arranged in a floral pattern.

"The polychrome mosaic is the most westerly example to have been found in a villa in Roman Britain," said Bill Horner, county archaeologist and historic environment manager at Devon County Council.

Horner added, "This, and the other trappings of Roman civilization and evidence of affluence that have been found, show how much even this far-flung part of the province had been integrated into the Roman Empire."

Photos released by officials show the mosaic, as well as ancient pottery and other artifacts unearthed after centuries underground.

SHAKESPEARE'S MISSING LONDON HOME PINPOINTED AFTER CENTURIES-LONG MYSTERY, RESEARCHER SAYS

The red, white and dark blue cubes were used to form a stylized flower with eight overlapping petals.

Alongside the villa, archaeologists excavated two additional stone buildings: one believed to have been a bathhouse and another that was likely used for agriculture.

Archaeologists also found a delicate copper-alloy bracelet, a fine silver-plated spoon and a beaker used for serving drinks, as well as a collection of pottery fragments and an engraved gemstone depicting the goddess Victory.

Britain was part of the Roman Empire from A.D. 43 until the early fifth century. Experts said the colorful mosaic is the westernmost example ever found at a Roman villa in Britain.

HIDDEN UNDERGROUND CHAMBER REVEALED BENEATH HOME OF LEGENDARY ROMAN EMPEROR

The discoveries indicate the villa was once home to a wealthy Roman family, archaeologists said.

Project leader Susan Greaney, an archaeology professor at the University of Exeter, said her team "did not expect to find such an elaborate bathhouse."

"At the outset, we knew this villa, and its surrounding working areas, was an important site for understanding the Romanization of Devon," she said in a release.

"But from day one, it has offered us a wealth of interesting and sometimes surprising finds in addition to this striking polychrome mosaic. ... This villa was undoubtedly home to people of wealth and high standing."

The site first came to light in 2004, when local metal detectorist John Hill discovered Roman remains.

Officials are now working to carefully transport the mosaic to the local Tiverton Museum of Mid-Devon Life.

The latest find is one of many remarkable Roman discoveries made across England in recent years.

Last summer, archaeologists uncovered an extensive 2,000-year-old Roman settlement in the Cotswolds after an amateur metal detectorist's chance discovery.

This summer, archaeologists working ahead of a British railway project unearthed a rare Roman coin and a trove of ancient artifacts.

item.title: Ariana Grande sets record straight after announcing break from spotlight
item.description: PR expert says Ariana Grande's strategic absence after her "Eternal Sunshine Tour" could build anticipation and make her return an event.
item.content:encoded:
Ariana Grande is taking control of her own narrative.

While performing in Chicago on Monday, the Grammy Award winner addressed concertgoers directly after news broke that she plans to take a break from all public appearances and performances once her "Eternal Sunshine Tour" wraps up next month.

"Sometimes when a story comes out that's not directly from me, things can get a little blown out of proportion, so I just wanted to speak to my fans directly tonight because I love you so much," Grande told the crowd, according to multiple videos shared on social media.

"The announcement that was made yesterday was not a reactive or impulsive thing. It was something that I had decided, it's a plan that I had quietly made a long time ago. It was a decision that was made from a thoughtful and empowered place. And I want you to know that many things can be true at the same time."

ARIANA GRANDE FIGHTS BACK AGAINST BODY-SHAMERS AS CRITICS COMMENT ON HER WEIGHT DURING 'WICKED' PRESS TOUR

Grande's comments came one day after her representative confirmed to People magazine that the singer will step away from the public eye for a while. 

"Ariana will be taking a step back from visibility after she completes the ‘Eternal Sunshine Tour’," Grande's representative told the outlet. "She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"This tour has been a beautiful experience for her. She loves her fans and has loved every minute of this tour so much," the representative added.

The planned hiatus is already affecting Grande's schedule. According to People, the singer will no longer appear in the West End revival of Stephen Sondheim's "Sunday in the Park with George" next summer.

Addressing fans in Chicago, Grande acknowledged that many had worried the decision was fueled by negativity.

"I just have to say that could not be more the f--- opposite," she said. "This is not what that is."

She continued, "Multiple things can be true at the same time: boundaries need to be set, human beings can need a break sometimes… and also, this can be and will continue to be the greatest experience of my professional and creative life."

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Grande ended the emotional moment by calling the tour "the most healing, beautiful, corrective, magnificent, special experience of my life."

While the singer insisted the break had been planned long before it became public, PR expert Steve Honig believes the timing could ultimately strengthen her career.

"Stepping back from the spotlight can strengthen Ariana Grande's brand because she has reached a level of stardom where she can take a break without hurting her career," Honig, founder of The Honig Company, told Fox News Digital. "In today's nonstop media environment, Grande's scarcity will build anticipation and give audiences a chance to miss her. From a public relations standpoint, a strategic absence can create more value than constant visibility, making her eventual return feel like an event."

According to Honig, only a select group of entertainers can successfully disappear from public view without losing momentum.

"Whether stepping away from the spotlight helps a celebrity's career depends largely on how established they are and the strength of their personal brand," he explained. "Celebrities who have reached high levels of fame can afford to take a break because they have built loyal audiences and lasting relevance. In many cases, absence really does make the heart grow fonder."

Grande's announcement follows months of online discussion surrounding her appearance, something the "Wicked: For Good" star has addressed publicly on multiple occasions.

Last year, Grande reshared a previous message on her Instagram Story urging people to stop commenting on others' bodies.

SUPERMODEL SLAMS GLP-1 TREND, SAYS WEIGHT LOSS SHOTS ARE A 'SMACK IN THE FACE' TO BODY POSITIVITY MOVEMENT

"Resharing this from last year as a loving reminder to all," she wrote alongside a clip of a December 2024 interview with Cynthia Erivo.

In the video, Grande reflected on growing up in the spotlight.

"I've been doing this in front of the public and been a specimen in a Petri dish really since I was 16 or 17, so I have heard it all," she said. "I've heard every version of it, of what's wrong with me, and then you fix it, and then it's wrong for different reasons."

She added that criticism about a person's appearance can be damaging regardless of their level of fame.

"It's hard to protect yourself from that noise," Grande said. "It's something that is uncomfortable no matter what scale you're experiencing it on."

Honig said Grande's previous comments underscore one of the biggest branding challenges celebrities face when public attention shifts away from their work.

"When the conversation shifts from a celebrity's work to their appearance, regaining control of the narrative becomes much more difficult because appearance becomes the basis for discussion," he said. "The best way to change the conversation is not by responding to every criticism, but by addressing the issue with facts and giving people something else to focus on."

He added that prolonged speculation can ultimately reshape how audiences perceive a celebrity if left unanswered.

"The biggest branding challenge is maintaining a clear and consistent brand identity when public attention is focused on the wrong thing," Honig said. "Instead of being known for their talent, the celebrity risks becoming associated with superficial distractions that dilute their brand."

Still, Honig believes Grande's decision to address the speculation directly during Monday's concert was the right move.

"In the majority of cases, it is better for a celebrity to directly address any sort of negative speculation," he said. "By doing this, the celebrity will pretty much shut down the speculation, replacing it with facts. Left unanswered, speculation often takes on a life of its own and can become accepted as truth simply through repetition."

For Grande, however, Honig believes the planned hiatus won't diminish her career in any way. 

"Stepping back only works when a celebrity has reached the point where they have earned the luxury of being missed," he said. "Ariana Grande is one of those celebrities."

As the PGA Tour regular season reaches its thrilling conclusion, players head to Greensboro, North Carolina, for the 2026 Wyndham Championship. First held in 1938, the Wyndham is the final chance for golfers to make the top 70 of the FedExCup standings and secure their spots in the upcoming playoffs.

Standing in the field's way is Sedgefield Country Club, a short par-70 Donald Ross venue under 7,100 yards that rewards strategy over strength. Drivers can be kept in check, but iron accuracy, smart placement, and clutch putting on fast Bermuda greens are non-negotiables for surviving Sedgefield.

'PAR TALK': MICHAEL THORBJORNSON 'FINALLY' ARRIVES, PATRICK CANTLAY'S GUTLESS DECISION, AND THE FEDEX CUP PLAYOFF BUBBLE

Even though this has been the golf betting year from hell, I'm officially on a heater after profiting for a second straight PGA TOUR event at last week's Rocket Classic. Unfortunately, I need to hit three straight outrights to get out of the hole: -49.79 units (u) this season.

For the Wyndham, I'm risking 2.06u on outrights and 3u on placements. Without further ado, here are my horses for the course at Sedgefield.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

The following odds are based on my previous bets on the golfers listed below. Subject to change.

🇰🇷 Tom Kim +3600 at DraftKings (0.56u) and Top-20 with ties +152 at Kalshi (0.75u)

🇰🇷 Sungjae Im +5100 at DraftKings (0.39u) and Top-20 with ties +165 at Kalshi (0.75u)

🇺🇸 Davis Thompson +5800 at DraftKings (0.34u) and Top-10 with ties +398 at Kalshi (0.25u)

🇺🇸 Ben Kohles +5800 at DraftKings (0.34u) and Top-20 with ties +207 at Kalshi (0.5u)

🇺🇸 Blades Brown +7694 (0.26u) and Top-20 with ties +252 (0.5u), both at Kalshi

🇺🇸 Billy Horschel +11500 at DraftKings (0.17u) and Top-20 with ties +398 at Kalshi (0.25u)

Simply put, Kim has longer odds than guys he is playing better than. In fact, the only reason Tom’s odds aren’t shorter is that he won too recently and the market doesn’t think he can win twice in a short span. But, winning begets more winning.

Furthermore, the South Korean is leading this field in total strokes gained (SG) over his last five starts, according to DataGolf.com. During that stretch, he has a third at the U.S. Open, a win at the Genesis Scottish Open and a T20 at the 3M Open in his last tournament.

Kim won the 2022 Wyndham on debut and withdrew last year in his only other visit to Sedgefield. Bermuda greens are his best putting surface over the last 12 months, per Betsperts Golf. He is leading this field in SG: Approach over the last 36 rounds and ranks third in Par 4 scoring. When you put all that together, anything above +3000 is a good bet for Kim.

It’s been a tough year for Im, especially with the irons, as he ranks 149th in SG: Approach on TOUR this season.

However, Sungjae has gained strokes on approach in five of his seven career Wyndhams. He’s made the cut in all seven; Im finished T14-or-better in four of his first five appearances at Sedgefield, with a T6 in 2019, T9 in 2020 and T2 in 2022.

And while Sungjae is having a down year by his standards, he does have several nice finishes, such as T4 at the Valspar Championship, T5 at the Truist Championship, T14 at the British Open and a T15 at the Rocket Classic his last time out.

Finally, Im’s odds at Bookmaker are +3919 at the time of writing, which is important because Bookmaker has a sharp golf betting market.

After cashing a top-20 ticket for me by tying for eighth at last week’s Rocket Classic, I’m investing in Thompson again at the Wyndham. He’s improved year over year in his four visits to Sedgefield: Missed cut in 2021, T22 in 2023, T12 in 2024 and T11 last year.

The Georgia Bulldog has gained strokes around-the-green in his four Wyndhams, and he has struggled chipping this year. Thompson has picked up strokes off-the-tee in his four appearances at Sedgefield and he’s gained strokes in driving accuracy in three straight.

Thompson ranks 123rd in putting on TOUR this season, but he has gained strokes on the greens in the last two Wyndhams. Again, the 27-year-old enters this week with good lead-in form: T7 at the 3M Open two weeks ago and T8 last week.

Kohles is first in my model at Betsperts Golf. He leads this field in driving accuracy over the last 36 rounds, ranks third in SG: Approach and eighth in Par 4 scoring. Over that span, Kohles has a T23 at the U.S. Open, T3 at the John Deere Classic, T15 at the ISCO Championship and ninth at the 3M Open.

While he has historically been a terrible putter, Kohles has gained strokes on the greens in five of his last six starts, including four straight. If he keeps that up, he’ll be in the mix at Sedgefield this weekend.

OUTKICK SPORTS CARTOON OF THE DAY

Because, again, Kohles is one of the most accurate drivers in golf and dialed in with his irons and putting, approach play and driving are the three most important skills for Sedgefield.

There has been a youth movement on TOUR in the last two weeks. Jackson Koivun, one of the best college golfers ever, and Michael Thorbjornsen, 2024 PGA TOUR University valedictorian, both broke through for their first wins on TOUR at the 3M Open and Rocket Classic in the past two tournaments.

Brown is another name golf fans should get used to. He is just 19 years old and received a special temporary membership June 2. Brown has been tearing it up on the Korn Ferry Tour and has finished T18-or-better in six of his eight starts on the PGA TOUR this year.

He’s gained strokes across the board (driving, irons, chipping and putting) in his last two PGA TOUR starts: T12 at the John Deere Classic and T11 at the Corales Puntacana Championship. Brown narrowly missed a putt to shoot a 59 at The American Express in his first start this year.

This is another guy with fantastic course history at Sedgefield. Horschel has six T11-or-better finishes in his past seven Wyndham and has gained strokes putting in his last five. Billy Ho has missed the cut in four of his last five starts, including last week’s Rocket Classic.

But Horschel had an eight-tournament streak of gaining strokes on the field with his irons snapped last week, and he’s gained strokes with driving accuracy in six straight, so he was hitting the ball well. Plus, Billy Ho has 10 international wins with eight on the PGA TOUR and two on the DP World (European) Tour.

The bottom line is Horschel’s win equity is much better than his betting odds indicate. He’s a proven winner who has recently flashed the skills needed to win at Sedgefield, hence his strong finishes here.

item.title: Navy's Blue Angels were the stars of the Seattle Seahawks' first 'Hard Knocks' episode: 'America!'
item.description: The Blue Angels stole the show during Seattle's first padded practice since Super Bowl LX, turning NFL training camp into a air show preview.
item.content:encoded:
The Seattle Seahawks are allowing the NFL's annual "Hard Knocks" series to take us behind the scenes and the first episode with the defending Super Bowl champions gave us a peek of the first day of training camp, the first day of padded practice, and the Navy's Blue Angels stealing the show.

The Blue Angels typically play no role in an NFL training camp.

But somehow, at the climax of Tuesday night's episode, there they were roaring across the sky over the Seahawks and making some of the millionaire professional athletes and coaches react like wide-eyed kids.

SEAHAWKS SUPER BOWL HERO DERICK HALL OPENS UP ABOUT HOW 'GOD' SAVED HIM FROM NEAR-CERTAIN DEATH

More of that in a minute. But firstly, you should know that it is rare for the defending Super Bowl champs to allow dozens of cameras to be placed throughout their training facility and have players and coaches mic'd up so the viewing public (and opponents) can watch their meetings and practices, while listening to typically private conversations.

But the Seahawks are graciously allowing it this year and we saw plenty in this episode, from insights on practice fights, to intel on contracts.

And then we got to Seattle's first padded practice. The last time the Seahawks put on their pads?

"In San Francisco" for Super Bowl LX, coach Mike Macdonald said.

The shot then cuts to the Seahawks, on their field in pads, thudding each other up and perhaps being a little more physical than that ... until you hear the roar of jet engines overhead.

Players and coaches look skyward and six blue and yellow F/A-18s scream past in formation, a trail of white smoke in their wake.

"Yes, America!" Macdonald exclaims. "Blue Angels, baby, let's go!"

"America!" linebacker Ernest Jones IV exclaims.

And this is the moment we see that admiring fans have come to watch the Seahawks practice. And the admiring Seahawks are instead watching the Blue Angels practice for their Aug. 1-2 Boeing Seafair Air Show.

"How can you not watch the Blue Angels?," Macdonald asks rhetorically.

The Navy flight that buzzed the Renton, Washington training facility on the Southeastern shore of Lake Washington lasted much of the football team's first padded practice.

It seemingly served as the soundtrack to the workout.

"Man, we got football, an air show ..." Jones said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

It was awesome. And when it was over, Macdonald gathered his players in a huddle and delivered a message.

"Tell you what, men, that was a helluva practice," the coach said, "Ain't it great to be back in pads, playing football? It doesn't get better than this, little Seahawks style, America. We got the freaking Blue Angeles!"

The annual HBO series will follow the Seahawks all the way through training camp, the preseason, and until the final roster cuts. The series airs every Tuesday evening and then streams after that.

This 2026 premiere was obviously a little different than most because this episode closed with about two solid minutes of the Blue Angels preparing for their flights instead of the Seahawks preparing for more football.

Priorities.

America.

item.title: Americans deserve to know healthcare prices before the final bill arrives
item.description: A 2025 poll shows 96% of Americans support healthcare price transparency as Congress works to make it law, with billions in potential savings.
item.content:encoded:
In an era of political gridlock, at least one clear area of bipartisan common ground continues to exist — the desire for real healthcare price transparency. In fact, a 2025 poll showed 96% of Americans across the political spectrum are in favor of the commonsense idea that you deserve to know the price of healthcare before receiving it. And finally, tangible progress is being made in both chambers of Congress to build upon numerous executive orders and Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) rules and make healthcare price transparency the law of the land.

But why is healthcare price transparency so important?

First, healthcare price transparency is a needed initial step to fix the broken healthcare market. It allows for better, more accurate price signals, empowering patients with key information that allows them to shop for non-emergent healthcare goods and services. It also puts public pressure on care providers to justify prices, which may or may not be reasonable. I say let the market work. Ultimately, this drives up competition, which — in turn — lowers prices. In every other industry, we’ve seen this benefit the American consumer — why not healthcare?

3 STEPS THAT COULD STOP FRAUD AND MAKE HEALTHCARE MORE AFFORDABLE FOR ALL AMERICANS

And it is no question that competition driven by transparency is needed. Currently, prices for the exact same procedure can range nearly 10 times, and even the same procedure within a given hospital can have wildly different prices based on backroom negotiations and often arbitrary price tags. But the problem is amplified when the prices not only differ within and across hospitals but are secret to those receiving, and ultimately paying for, the care until the bill arrives weeks to months later. With over 40% of Americans with healthcare debt and more than 40 million Americans on high-deductible health insurance plans, the opaque nature of healthcare billing is simply unacceptable.

Second, we spend about one in every five dollars on healthcare in our economy. That’s a huge amount of money -– about $5.3 trillion. But inherently, spending so much money on healthcare isn’t bad — the better question is: what do we get for the money we spend?

We don’t know.

And a large proportion of our country’s spending is healthcare coverage, including over 150 million Americans who have insurance through their employers. Healthcare is one of the largest costs for employers, if not the largest. But even they don’t know what they get for the money they spend for their employees, nor do they know the price tag of healthcare goods and services up front. And are their employees healthier?

MEDICARE IS ONE OF AMERICA’S GREATEST SUCCESSES — AND A FISCAL TIME BOMB

Healthcare price transparency can improve employer plan management and strategy, removing one element of the "healthcare unknown" and eliminating bureaucratic and inefficient frustrations and waste. The focus for employers can then move to demanding insights on quality of care, a logical next step to build upon price transparency. Healthcare price transparency is a signal that secrecy within healthcare will no longer be tolerated. By marrying both transparent prices and the push for transparency around the clinical outcomes most important to patients, employers can ensure they are getting the most value for their money spent.

And this doesn’t just help employers. Savings on employer health insurance plans mean more money in employee pockets through higher take-home wages not spent on coverage. With a family of four spending about $27,000 per year on health insurance, that’s a lot of money families across America desperately need.

Lastly, healthcare price transparency efforts will not only help everyday Americans today but accelerate innovation. When competition exists, innovation follows, as organizations try to differentiate themselves and get an edge over our competitors. From care delivery model improvements, including the use of AI, to entrepreneurs making the healthcare price transparency data easier for everyday Americans to quickly digest, the possibilities are numerous.

Not only does healthcare price transparency give power back to the healthcare consumer, but the data on savings are clear. Studies demonstrate the potential savings are in the billions of dollars, with one study from the University of Minnesota estimating savings between $17 billion to $80 billion. Another study from Brown University estimates about $120 billion (with a plausible range of $25 billion to $270 billion) of savings over time.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

The evidence continues to grow in support of healthcare price transparency. It’s a bold, necessary start in "fixing" healthcare. So, now Congress must act.

It is past time for healthcare price transparency to be the law of the land, not just a collection of executive orders and CMS rules. And nearly all of America agrees.

item.title: 5 reasons more Americans are cutting off their own parents, according to psychologist
item.description: A psychologist identifies five key drivers of family estrangement, from political differences and social media influence to therapy culture and partners.
item.content:encoded:
Cutting off family members is becoming more and more common, leading experts to consider the drivers of the division.

A 2025 YouGov survey found that 38% of U.S. adults are estranged from at least one family member, including siblings, parents, children or grandparents.

Based on his research and work in the field of family estrangement, Dr. Richard L. Blake, a British psychologist and author based in Austin, Texas, shared the following five factors that he believes commonly contribute to fractured family relationships.

'DOORMAT MOM' CUT OFF BY DAUGHTER AMID ESTRANGEMENT TREND: ‘COMPLETELY BLINDSIDED’

A longstanding study of more than 2,000 mother-adult child relationships found that "value dissimilarity" was a strong predictor of estrangement, suggesting that differing beliefs may play a large role in family rifts.

"That could be political values, that could be gender ideology," Blake told Fox News Digital.

"There were people more likely to cut off someone for having a different opinion than for people who have done serious violent crimes," he said. "So certainly, political differences are a big problem."

Heavy social media use has been linked to poorer parent-child relationships. A study of nearly 9,800 teens found that spending more than two hours a day on social media was linked to significantly greater odds of negative relationships with one or both parents.

Blake believes social media may also normalize family estrangement by exposing users to viral "no contact" stories and encouraging what he described as "word-of-mouth mimicry."

SECOND LADY USHA VANCE GETS CANDID ABOUT NEW BABY, JUGGLING FOUR CHILDREN AND MOTHERHOOD

"Someone might see a video on TikTok — 'I cut off my parents, and I'm much happier now. They were toxic narcissistic boundary crossers. And now I'm great,'" he said. "And people mimic that. Or they think, 'Oh, this person's getting a lot of attention.'"

Although he acknowledged that there are no long-term studies that have definitively documented an increase, "that doesn't mean absence of evidence isn't evidence of absence."

According to Blake, society has shifted away from what he described as a "dignity culture" toward one that places greater value on "victim culture."

"So now it's a race to the bottom," he said. "If you don't have enough victim status because of the way you were born, you can create a victim status by suggesting your parents abused you or neglected you … and therefore you have value, a reason to cut them off."

The expert also pointed to what he described as "therapy culture," claiming that changing attitudes toward trauma and abuse have influenced how some people view relationships with their parents.

"Another justification is, ‘I cut off my parents to protect my mental health’ — and this is a sort of false belief," he told Fox News Digital. "There is this huge bias that if you're struggling in your adult life, it must be because your parents did something they shouldn't or didn't do something."

Blake argued that family relationships remain one of the strongest protective factors for mental health.

"Families are one of the most evidence-based buffers against mental illness," he said. "There’s this myth that families are not important."

The psychologist pointed to a well-known Minnesota study of adopted twins, which found that twins often resembled their biological parents more than the adoptive parents who raised them.

BECKHAM FAMILY FEUD: WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT BROOKLYN'S WIFE, BILLIONAIRE HEIRESS NICOLA PELTZ

He also cited a 2024 study led by German sociologist Karsten Hank, which found that adults estranged from parents or siblings reported lower life satisfaction and more depressive symptoms than those who maintained family relationships.

"So it seems like it's certainly a health event for parents who get cut off, and it's probably a negative health event for the kids or the adult children who are doing the cutoff," he said. "It's this lie they're getting sold on social media: ‘Cut off your parents and your mental health will be better.’"

The way families communicate during conflict can determine whether disagreements escalate into long-term estrangement, according to Blake.

It’s important to listen first, he said, noting that "hostage negotiation" can be useful in these scenarios.

"[That means] listening to the other person and then repeating back what they said as you understood it and validating that … and then waiting until that person's really finished before you give your side of it."

Blake also raised the issue of "moralized language," or "therapy words" that get thrown at parents — "such as abuse, toxic, boundaries, narcissists, gaslighting."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"When you use moralized language like that, compromise becomes far more difficult," he said.

"So I tell parents to pause before they really react ... and then say back, ‘Okay, you've used the word toxic. Can you describe the behavior or behaviors that you consider to be toxic?’ Then you're dealing with facts and events, rather than who’s a better person or who's the worst person."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

The psychologist also recommends starting with "I" statements rather than using the word "you," and also avoid using the words "always" and "never."

Finally, Blake said that outside influences — including romantic partners and evolving parenting philosophies — can also contribute to family estrangement.

Those outside influences may differ by gender, he noted, with romantic partners often playing a larger role for men.

As an example, Blake pointed to public figures such as Brooklyn Beckham and Prince Harry, suggesting that romantic partners can sometimes influence how people view their relationships with family members.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Conflicting parenting philosophies may also strain family relationships, as adult children and grandparents sometimes disagree over how children should be raised, according to Blake.

"Parenting styles are obviously different, and they've changed a lot over the last few years," he said.

"If you look at the outcomes of the gentle parenting or the permissive parenting that we've slipped into, we have the most mentally ill generation in history, the least fit for adulthood," Blake suggested. "Perhaps we should be learning from our grandparents more than the therapists."

item.title: Back to school should not mean back to fear for Jewish students
item.description: FBI statistics show Jews face 70% of religion-based hate crimes despite being 2% of the population, with 10% of those crimes occurring in schools.
item.content:encoded:
It’s back to school time and many Jewish families are worried about much more than just shopping for new shoes and school supplies. They are concerned that their children may not be safe because they are Jewish.

Alongside math and reading, school is where children learn where they fit into society and whether the surrounding adults will protect them, but the recent rise in antisemitic threats and violence is putting all of that in jeopardy.

According to the New York Police Department, antisemitic hate crimes increased by 8.5% in New York City in the first seven months of 2026. The majority of hate crimes in the city were anti-Jewish, despite Jewish New Yorkers being only a tenth of the population.

ANTISEMITISM CONTROVERSY ERUPTS AT ELITE NY HIGH SCHOOL AFTER ISRAEL FLYER FOUND IN URINAL

But it’s not just a New York problem.

Recent FBI statistics show that, although Jews make up only 2% of the U.S. population, they were the victims of 16% of all reported hate crimes and nearly 70% of all religion-based hate crimes.

And 10% of those crimes happened in schools. Antisemitic incidents at K-12 schools have increased 434% since 2020.

While rising antisemitism has resulted in real-world violence that directly impacts the Jewish community, it is a problem for our entire society and requires a whole-of-society response, with our cultural and political leaders stepping up.

CHRISTIAN LEADERS HOLD EMERGENCY SUMMIT IN JERUSALEM TO CONFRONT GLOBAL RISE IN ANTISEMITISM

Online platforms must enforce their own rules against incitement and threats. Research has found that 74% of Americans who encountered antisemitism saw or heard it online or on social media. Two thirds of Jewish adults who experienced this did not report it because they did not think anything would be done.

Imagine how much more profound this is for both Jewish and non-Jewish children. Students often carry what they see online into their real lives. A culture that excuses online antisemitism eventually meets students at the school locker, the bus stop and the classroom.

Schools cannot solve every social failure, but they can set the standard for how a free society responds to hate.

The U.S. Department of Education issued a letter reminding schools "Title VI protects all students, including students who are or are perceived to be Jewish, from discrimination," and that "schools must take immediate and appropriate action to respond to harassment that creates a hostile environment."

DOJ SUES UCLA OVER ALLEGED ‘JUDENREIN’ CONDITIONS DURING ANTI-ISRAEL ENCAMPMENT

SIGN UP FOR ANTISEMITISM EXPOSED NEWSLETTER

Administrators should say plainly that antisemitism is unacceptable, whether it appears as a threat, a slur, a swastika, harassment over Jewish identity or intimidation tied to Israel or Zionism.

Further, education must be more than a one-off assembly after an incident. Students should learn what antisemitism is, how it mutates across political movements, conspiracy theories and social media trends and why targeting Jews corrodes civic life for everyone.

Schools and law enforcement should coordinate before a crisis. Every school that serves Jewish students should have a clear plan for reporting threats, preserving evidence, communicating with families and protecting students who are targeted. This means treating credible threats and hate crimes as serious matters from the start.

Importantly, safety has to be treated as a public responsibility, not a private surcharge on Jewish families. My organization, Teach Coalition, has found that Jewish schools spend more than $400,000 a year on security, more than $1,000 per student, money that could otherwise support teachers, scholarships, mental health services and academic programs.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Public funding must meet the scale of the threat. The FEMA Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP) helps nonprofits at high risk of terrorist attack, providing $274.5 million for security measures last year. But only 27% of 2025 applications were approved.

If threats are rising and three-quarters of qualified applicants are turned away, Congress should quadruple NSGP funding to a billion dollars and make the process faster and more predictable.

Leaders should stop treating antisemitism as someone else’s problem. School boards, governors, mayors, clergy, union leaders, parent associations and cultural figures all shape the norms children absorb.

A whole-of-society response means better education, stronger security, lawful accountability, responsible technology and the moral clarity to say that Jewish students should never have to hide who they are in order to learn.

item.title: NCAA softball player reveals alleged encounter with pro-trans counterprotesters at Sophie Cunningham rally
item.description: Kendall Kotzmacher alleges a counterprotester with a megaphone told her she "should've been aborted" at the Sophie Cunningham rally in Minneapolis.
item.content:encoded:
Kendall Kotzmacher returned from college to her home state on Sunday to attend a Sophie Cunningham rally in Minneapolis.

She made the trip home to Minnesota just more than year after her final high school softball game in the state ended in a championship defeat to a transgender pitcher, who also hit a double to help win the game.

Kotzmacher, who is set to play for Colorado Christian this upcoming year, stood alongside Riley Gaines, Michelle Tafoya and Jennifer Sey, as they led the the third rally in support of Cunningham in the span of one week. Counterprotesters had appeared the previous two rallies for Cunningham. But Sunday saw a different degree of agitation compared to the first two.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM RALLY ROCKS WNBA GAME AS 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS' ACTIVISTS FACE COUNTERPROTEST

Kotzmacher was caught right in the middle of it.

A pro-transgender protester at the rally allegedly approached with a megaphone and unleashed insults at the group. One remark was directed at Kotzmacher in front of her mother and sister.

"He had a megaphone and was just yelling everything about how awful people we are," Kotzmacher told Fox News Digital. "At one point, I got told that I should’ve been aborted when I was younger."

Kotzmacher said she had previously received hostile messages online after speaking publicly about competing against a transgender athlete. Sunday marked the first time she encountered that level of hostility in person.

"I’ve gotten so many hate texts, death threats, people commenting on my posts, all of that stuff," she said. "So at this point, I’m kind of used to it, but it was definitely weird for them to be able to hear it and be like, ‘Oh, people are actually like this. Someone has enough to say this out loud to a person.’

"They have no rebuttal to what we’re standing for," she added. "They have nothing to go against what we’re trying to say, and so they just go back to calling us names."

The confrontation allegedly grew more physical when Gaines arrived shortly before the game. Kotzmacher said Gaines had initially planned to attend the entire rally but delayed her appearance because of safety concerns.

Kotzmacher alleged police officers nearby did not intervene and said a male bystander started to push people around.

VALKYRIES COACH NATALIE NAKASE DEFENDS TRANS ATHLETES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS AS CULTURE WAR ENGULFS WNBA

"A man, just a bystander, had to push him out of the way while the cops watched all this happen," she said.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Minneapolis Police Department for a response.

Kotzmacher said she and her family took precautions before traveling into Minneapolis, including parking near the arena and making sure no one walked alone. Once she joined the larger crowd, however, she felt safer.

"I remember talking to my mom, and I was like, ‘Okay, we need to make sure that we’re being smart. We’re parking near where we’re walking, making sure that we’re never alone,’" she said. "Once we got there and I was in a big enough group, I was like, ‘Okay, I’m with a crowd. I’m going to be okay.’"

Another women's sports activist who was there, Amy Sousa, had her own experience with the counterprotesters, and even claims to have had a civil conversation with one.

"The opposition in Minneapolis showed up as they always do, trying to drown out women’s voices with megaphones and sound machines. This time, as I calmly stood in front of this woman with her megaphone, I simply asked her to tell me what she thinks I believe so I could tell her what I actually believe," Sousa said.

"After explaining that I’m a Democrat and my position is pro-women and girls on the basis of sex she admitted 'that’s a little bit different,' than what she thought. She ended up agreeing with me. My colleague Kara Dansky has always said, 'if we can be heard, we will win.' And this conversation proves that’s true.

And despite the confrontations, Kotzmacher said rally supporters received more positive feedback, privately.

"There were so many people that were supportive of us," she said. "I got so many compliments on our shirt. Everyone got so many compliments on what we’re doing. But in the media, they go to show everyone against us, which is kind of funny to see, because if you were there, it wasn’t that way at all."

The dueling demonstrations continued inside Target Center. Cunningham was booed when she touched the ball, while fans wearing shirts supporting transgender athletes appeared throughout the arena.

Kotzmacher, who sat in the upper level, alleged the arena’s video board repeatedly featured fans with pro-transgender messages but avoided showing Cunningham supporters and their shirts.

"Every time that the jumbotron was on, it was showing people with pro-trans signs or shirts, or anything like that, of them cheering," she said. "Even when Sophie was getting booed, they would put the jumbotron on people booing her."

RILEY GAINES SAYS TARGET CENTER STAFFER TRIED TO SHUT DOWN HER SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SIGN

Kotzmacher argued that the presentation did not reflect the full reaction inside the arena.

"There were so many people that cheered for her, but the media only paid attention to the negative parts," she said.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Lynx for a response.

She also said the atmosphere became more welcoming after rally attendees entered the building. Fans stopped Kotzmacher to praise her shirt, while others asked to take pictures with Gaines.

"Once we got in there, most people stopped," Kotzmacher said of the hostility. "So many people stopped us to say, ‘This is great what you’re doing,’ or even to take pictures with Riley. So once we got in, it was really supportive."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

But the hostility resurfaced after the Lynx defeated the Fever. Kotzmacher said people leaving the arena pointed, laughed and taunted her group over Indiana’s loss and Cunningham’s performance.

"Someone’s like, ‘Ha, you lost,’" Kotzmacher said. "We got pointed at or laughed at. Individuals were like, ‘Ha, you guys lost. How many points did Sophie have today?’"

Kotzmacher thought back to her final high school softball game in the state championship.

The trans pitcher held Kotzmacher's team to just two runs on seven innings, then hit a double in the final inning to set up the winning run.

Kotzmacher fell into her little sister's arms sobbing after the walk-off loss. The loss later ignited the feud between Simone Biles and Riley Gaines last June after Gaines posted about the championship that same day.

Kotzmacher has since gone on to do multiple televised interviews about her experience, and has signed a brand ambassador deal with XX-XY Athletics as an NIL athlete.

Now, as Kotzmacher continues her college softball career at Colorado Christian, she plans to continue advocating for the protection of women's sports.
